chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, our matter is veiled, masked by the Covenant; so whoever tears the veil upon us, Allah will humble him.

key_terms.أَمْرُنَا: Our matter/affair (referring to the Imams' authority and presence)
key_terms.بِالْمِيثَاقِ: By the Covenant (divine promise or bond)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Imams' matter being veiled by the Covenant?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the doctrine of *al-Mithaq* (the Divine Covenant) as the metaphysical basis for the Imams' concealment (*ghaybah*), ensuring their authority remains protected from premature exposure. It highlights that the 'humbling' of those who 'tear the veil' serves as a divine safeguard against those who might disrupt the esoteric order or claim authority without legitimate standing. This concept is central to Twelver Shia theology, distinguishing the hidden Imam's presence from mere absence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Khalid Bin Najeeh, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Our<sup>asws</sup> matter is veiled, masked by the Covenant. So the one who tears (the veil) upon us, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Disgrace him’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Khalid ibn Nujayh from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Our cause is hidden and veiled by the (Divine) covenant.
Whoever disregards it against us Allah will humiliate him.”
